name: Tessera Overwatch Platform OWP-3 'Panopticon'
description:
A semi-autonomous sniper platform that combines a precision railgun with an AI-assisted targeting suite. The OWP-3 can be deployed in a fixed position and left to operate autonomously for up to 72 hours, using its sensor array to identify and engage designated target profiles without human intervention.

The Panopticon's AI targeting operates on a strict engagement protocol — it will only fire on targets matching pre-loaded biometric profiles, and it requires BCI confirmation from an authorized operator before engaging unregistered targets. In autonomous mode, the weapon achieves a first-round hit probability of 94% at ranges under 2km.

Tessera markets the OWP-3 as a force multiplier for corporate perimeter defense, but its autonomous capability has raised concerns even within GLMZ's permissive regulatory environment. Several municipal councils have attempted to ban autonomous lethal platforms, only to discover that Tessera's legal team had preemptively secured exemptions through corporate sovereignty provisions.
legality: Corporate sovereign territory only — banned in public zones
specifications:
caliber: 4mm tungsten flechette
effective_range: 200-2,500 meters
rate_of_fire: 1 round per 5 seconds
capacity: 20-round sealed magazine
weight: 32 kg (platform), 12 kg (power unit)
power_source: Compact fusion cell, 72 hours standby / 40 shots active
tactical_use: The Panopticon is deployed to establish persistent overwatch without committing personnel. Corporate security details place OWP-3 units at choke points, rooftops, and perimeter positions where they function as automated sentinels. The weapon's AI can track multiple targets simultaneously and prioritize engagement based on threat assessment algorithms. In contested zones, a single Panopticon can deny access to an area more effectively than a four-person sniper team.
cultural_context: The existence of autonomous kill platforms has created a new form of urban anxiety in GLMZ. Residents in corporate-adjacent zones speak of 'watched streets' — thoroughfares where Panopticons are suspected to be deployed. Some communities have developed informal networks that track and share suspected OWP-3 positions, though Tessera's legal department aggressively pursues anyone who publishes confirmed locations.
story_hooks: A Panopticon unit has gone rogue — still active after its authorization expired, still engaging targets matching a biometric profile that was supposed to be purged. The targets are all employees of a single corporation.
Someone has hacked an OWP-3's targeting protocol and loaded civilian biometric data. The weapon is now an indiscriminate killer hiding somewhere in the upper tiers.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Portable Fusion Battery PFB-2

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular sniper platform with a distinctly predatory aesthetic—part precision instrument, part autonomous hunter. The railgun barrel dominates the upper profile, extending from a compact receiver housing. The entire assembly sits atop a stabilization gimbal with three articulated servo mounts, giving it an insectoid quality. Sensor clusters bulge from the sides like compound eyes.
physical_description.dimensions: Platform body: 89cm length × 34cm width × 52cm height. Railgun barrel: 127cm from breach to muzzle. Footprint of stabilization base: 60cm × 60cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and imposing—32kg platform weight demands secure mounting. The power unit (12kg) is a separate dense block suggesting extreme energy density. Feels engineered for permanence rather than portability.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced composite frame with steel barrel assembly. Sensor housings in smart polymer with embedded conductors. Gimbal joints are hardened steel with ceramic bearings.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite with brushed gunmetal accents on barrel and mechanical joints. Weatherproof coating shows micro-abrasion patterns from deployment. Sensor domes have a faint iridescent quality under angled light—anti-glint treatment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray dominant, with black composite sections and deep blue accent strips along sensor arrays. Tessera branding in cold silver on the receiver block.
physical_description.grip_texture: No traditional grip—the platform is mounted, not handheld. Control surfaces feature rubberized keypads with tactile feedback for field calibration. Mounting points have textured steel flanges.
distinctive_features: Hyperlinear railgun barrel with precision rifling visible at muzzle
Three-axis gimbal stabilization system with servo motors visibly articulated
Sensor cluster array: LIDAR dome, thermal imaging window, optical tracking system stacked along right flank
Magazine cartridge on left side—sealed 20-round tungsten flechette magazine with status indicators
Cable management: thick fiber-optic tether for BCI operator link, power umbilical to fusion cell
Cooling radiator fins along rear housing—suggests active thermal management during sustained fire
Tessera corporate logo and model designation stamped in gray on black composite nameplate
LED status indicators: green (standby), amber (tracking), red (target lock) arranged vertically on rear
Modular quick-release mounts at base for rapid repositioning
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA embossed in sans-serif on upper receiver block. OWP-3 'PANOPTICON' designation in smaller text below. Serial plate mounted on gimbal base housing—brushed steel with laser-etched identifier. Regulatory exemption number engraved beneath barrel—a legal scar on the weapon itself.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained, meticulous. These units are expensive corporate assets. Likely shows field use—dust accumulation in gimbal joints, minor scuff marks on composite from transport cases, faint discoloration on barrel from thermal cycling. Optics may show faint condensation halos from climate stress. Despite wear, visibly maintained to operational standards.
